title: The uncle, Thursday
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Thursday, after the shop. The uncle asleep in the chair. Wood doesn't draw him asleep; he did that once. He draws the chair's shadow, long, on the gravel, with the line's shadow in it. Gully sees the drawing and understands it and says nothing.

panels.composition: Evening. The UNCLE asleep in the chair by the shack. The chair's shadow long across the gravel. GULLY closing the shack. WOOD, BARNABY.

image.prompt: an old man asleep in a lawn chair beside a shack at evening with the chair's shadow stretched long across the gravel, a teenager closing up, a young man and a dog, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The shadow on the gravel: the chair, the man, the thin line of the oxygen tube, all in shadow.

image.prompt: close on a long shadow across gravel of a man in a lawn chair with the thin line of a tube in it, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The pad: the shadow only. No chair. No man. The strip draws what the light did.

image.prompt: close on a drawing pad with an ink drawing of a long shadow of a chair and a seated figure on gravel, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Gully looking at the pad over Wood's shoulder. Understanding it. Saying nothing. Locking the shack. Thursday.

image.prompt: a stocky teenager looking over a young man's shoulder at a drawing of a shadow, then turning to lock a shack door, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Thursday. The shadow only. Gully understands.
